Following the execution of Guevara in La Higuera in 1967, the Bolivian military faced a logistical nightmare: they needed to provide irrefutable proof of death to international intelligence agencies without leaving a body that could serve as a pilgrimage site. After a secret midnight burial beneath the Vallegrande airstrip, a specific set of artifacts were secured.
These artifacts were initially flown to Buenos Aires so that the Argentine Federal Police could compare notes. In 1968, in a stunning act of espionage, the Bolivian Minister of the Interior, Antonio Arguedas, smuggled these items (along with a famous secret diary) out of the country to Havana. While the rest of the remains stayed hidden for thirty years, these artifacts arrived in Cuba decades earlier, where they were received by a somber Fidel Castro. What artifacts and how were they used to confirm his death?
